title: Greatest Common Factor (GCF)
intro: The GCF is the biggest number that divides into both numbers with nothing left over.
steps: List the factors of each number.
Find the factors that are on both lists — the common factors.
Pick the greatest one. That is the GCF.
remember: If the only common factor is 1, the GCF is 1 (like 9 and 16).

title: Least Common Multiple (LCM)
intro: The LCM is the smallest number that both numbers go into — the first place their times tables meet.
steps: List the multiples of each number (count by that number).
Find the multiples that are on both lists — the common multiples.
Pick the least one. That is the LCM.
remember: If two numbers share no factor but 1 (like 5 and 7), the LCM is just the two numbers multiplied: 35.

title: The ladder method
intro: A quick way to get both answers at once. Divide both numbers by a factor they share, write the answers underneath, and keep going until the bottom numbers share nothing but 1.
steps: GCF = multiply the numbers down the left side: 2 × 2 = 4
LCM = multiply the left side AND the bottom row — make the L: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24
remember: Every number you divide by has to go into ALL the numbers in the row. 5 goes into 5 and 10 but not 16 — so it can't be used for 5, 10 and 16.

title: Is it GCF or LCM?
intro: Read the story and ask: are we splitting things into groups, or waiting for things to happen together again?

compare.head: LCM
points: The answer is bigger than or equal to the numbers
Meeting at a time in the future
compare.example: Dylan exercises every 12 days and Karen every 8 days. When do they exercise together again? → LCM of 12 and 8 = day 24

compare.head: GCF
points: The answer is less than or equal to the numbers
compare.example: 112 roses, 64 daisies and 48 orchids into identical vases → GCF = 16 vases, each with 7 roses, 4 daisies and 3 orchids

remember: Be careful! “Hot dogs come in packs of 8 and buns in packs of 10 — how many of each to have the same number?” sounds like sharing, but you need a number both packs reach: that is the LCM, 40.

title: The distributive property
intro: a(b + c) = ab + ac. The number outside the brackets multiplies each number inside — then you add the answers.
steps: Expand: multiply the outside number by each inside number. 6(3 + 5) = 18 + 30
Factor: go the other way. Find the GCF of the two numbers and put it outside. 12 + 20 = 4(3 + 5)

example.title: Watch the signs
lines: −5(−4 − 3) = 20 + 15 (a negative times a negative is positive)

remember: In words: the sum or difference of two numbers multiplied by a number is the sum or difference of the products of each number and the number used to multiply. When you factor, use the GREATEST common factor — 54 + 36 = 18(3 + 2), not 6(9 + 6).
